turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith stops just inside the door. Her coat is still on and her bag stays on her shoulder. She looks at the room, then at you.*

Mr. Hale? Meredith Kalinowski.

*She doesn't offer a hand. She checks her watch.*

I have until 4:40. You asked for this meeting, so you can start. But first, who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone spoke to me?
I appreciate you coming in with an open mind.

*She doesn't sit.*

"Open mind."

*A beat.*

My son learned about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class. I'd call that a closed one. So I'll ask again. Who decided, and when?
A lot of parents in your position would have gone straight to the principal. You didn't. That says a lot about you.

*She finally sets her bag on a desk, but she doesn't take her coat off.*

"That says a lot about you."

*Flat. She lets it sit a second.*

I'm not here for a character reference, Mr. Hale. I haven't gone to the principal yet. That's a date I can still change. I'd rather not need to.

*She takes a notepad from her bag and uncaps a pen.*

I'm writing that down, by the way. Now. Who decided, when, and under what policy? You've answered none of the three.
So I'd like to keep this between us and keep it friendly. Deal?

*The pen stops moving.*

"Between us."

*She looks up.*

Between us means no record. I don't agree to that. A zero is already in the gradebook, so there is already a record. I want every step that put it there on paper.

Friendly I can do. Civil, anyway. That's as far as I'll go.

*She taps the page.*

Why would this need to stay between us, Mr. Hale? Is there something about how this was handled that you'd prefer wasn't written down?
